Rashi on Shabbat 22a:1:1.hebrew: פסולה - דלא שלטא בה עינא למעלה מכ' אמה, וליכא פרסומי ניסא:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:1:1.english: Is invalid - For the eye does not reach it above twenty cubits, and there is no publicizing of the miracle.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:1:2.hebrew: כסוכה וכמבוי - דתנן בהו בהדיא בעירובין ומסכת סוכה, דפסילי:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:1:2.english: Like a sukkah and like an alleyway - For we learned explicitly regarding them in [Tractate] Eruvin and Tractate Sukkah that they are invalid.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:2:1.hebrew: מצוה להניחה - בחצר או ברה"ר, בטפח הסמוך לפתח; שאם ירחיקנו להלן מן הפתח, אינו ניכר שבעה"ב הניחו שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:2:1.english: It is a mitzvah to place it - [Whether] in the courtyard or in the public domain, within the handbreadth adjacent to the entrance; for if one distances it further from the entrance, it is not evident that the homeowner placed it there.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:2:2.english: On the right - Upon entering his house, to the right.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:2:3.hebrew: מזוזה - קי"ל דבימין, דכתיב: "ביתך" — דרך ביאתך, וכי עקר אינש כרעיה, דימנא עקר ברישא:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:2:3.english: Mezuza - We hold that [it is placed] on the right, as it is written: "Your house [beitekha]" — the way of your entry [bi'atekha]; and when a person lifts his foot, he lifts the right [foot] first.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:3:2.hebrew: במה ששפך - בידו ששפך בה, ולא ברגלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:3:2.english: With that which he poured - With his hand, with which he poured, and not with his foot.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:1.english: Decorations of a sukkah - Fruits that they hang in it for decoration.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:2.english: Master of Abraham - This is an expression of astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:3.hebrew: תלי - סוכה, דתניא בברייתא בהדיא, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:3.english: He makes dependent - [The case of] sukka, which is explicitly taught in a baraita, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:4.hebrew: בדלא תניא - בנר חנוכה, דמימרא דרב אסי הוא ואינו ברייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:4.english: Upon that which was not taught - Upon the Hanukkah light, for it is a statement of Rav Assi and is not a baraita.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:5.english: And adorned it with tapestries - He decorated it with colored hangings, which they call ouvrez [embroidered fabrics].

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:6.hebrew: התנה עליהן - במס' ביצה (דף ל:) אוקימנא: באומר "איני בודל מהן כל בין השמשות של קידוש יו"ט ראשון", דלא חל עלייהו קדושה כלל; אבל תנאי אחר אינו מועיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:6.english: [If] he stipulated with regard to them - In Tractate Beitza (30b), we established [this as referring to] one who says: "I do not separate myself from them throughout the twilight of the sanctification of the first day of the Festival," so that sanctity does not take effect upon them at all; but another stipulation is not effective.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:7.english: The father of them all - That all of them should be derived from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:8.hebrew: דם - כיסוי הדם, דנפקא לן מקרא "ושפך וכסה", ומפרש בה טעמא: שלא יהיו מצות בזויות עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:4:8.english: Blood - [This refers to] the covering of the blood, which we derive from the verse, "and he shall pour out... and cover," and [the baraita] explains the reason for it: so that mitzvot should not be contemptible to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:1.hebrew: מנר לנר - דחנוכה, כדמפרש טעמא לקמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:1.english: From [one] lamp to [another] lamp - [Lamps] of Hanukkah, as the reason is explained below.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:2.hebrew: מתירין - להטיל ציצית מטלית ישן לטלית חדש, ובמנחות מפרש טעמא דמאן דאסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:2.english: [One may] untie - To attach tzitzit from an old garment to a new garment. And in Menachot, the reason of the one who forbids is explained.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:3.hebrew: הלכ' כר"ש - דאמר דבר שאין מתכוין מותר, ואע"ג דקעביד חריץ, והוי תולדה דחורש או בונה. ומשום דהילכתא כרב באיסורי בכוליה הש"ס, בר מהני תלת, נקטינהו גבי הדדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:5:3.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - For he said that an unintentional act is permitted, even though he makes a furrow, which is a derivative [labor] of plowing or building. And because the halakha follows Rav in matters of prohibition throughout the entire Talmud, except for these three, they cited them together.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:6:1.english: All matters of the Master - [The Master was] Rabbah bar Nachmani.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:6:2.english: To make a furrow - [This] is our reading.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:7:1.hebrew: טעמא דרב - מנר לנר משום ביזוי מצוה — שמדליק קיסם שאינה מן המצוה מנר של מצוה, וממנו מדליק השאר:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:7:1.english: Rav's reason - [For prohibiting lighting] from lamp to lamp is due to contempt for the mitzvah — for one lights a splinter, which is not [part] of the mitzvah, from a mitzvah lamp, and from it lights the rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:7:2.english: Weakening - For it appears like one who takes [its] light and draws off a bit of the moisture of its oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 22a:7:3.hebrew: משרגא לשרגא - מביא נר אצל נר — ושתיהן של מצוה — ולא בקיסם:
Rashi on Shabbat 22a:7:3.english: From lamp to lamp - He brings [one] lamp next to [another] lamp — and both of them are of the mitzvah — and not with a wood chip.

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:1:1.hebrew: נר חנוכה שהניחה למעלה מכ' אמה פסולה כסוכה וכמבוי - וא"ת: הוה ליה למימר "ימעט", כמו גבי מבוי, דאמר התם: מבוי דרבנן — תני תקנתא? ואיכא למימר: דנקט "פסולה" משום דבעי למימר "כסוכה", שהיא מן התורה. אי נמי, לא רצה להאריך: יכבנה וימעטנה ויחזור וידליקנ', דלמעטה ולהניחה כמו שהיא דולקת אי אפשר, כדמוכח לקמן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:1:1.english: A Hanukkah lamp that one placed above twenty cubits is invalid, like a sukkah and like an alleyway - And if you say: It should have said "let him lower it," as in the case of an alleyway, where [the Gemara] says there: "[Since] an alleyway is rabbinic, it teaches a remedy"? And one can say: It stated "invalid" because it wanted to say "like a sukkah," which is from the Torah. Alternatively, it did not want to elaborate: "He must extinguish it, lower it, and rekindle it," for to lower it and leave it as it is while lit is impossible, as is proven later.

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:1.hebrew: סוכה תניא - משמע דטעמא דנויי סוכה משום ביזוי מצוה. וקשה לר"י: בפרק כירה (לקמן שבת דף מה. ושם) משמע דטעמא משום מיגו דאיתקצי למצותה! ותירץ: דצריכי לתרווייהו; דמשום דאיתקצי למצותה לא הוה אסרינן בחולו של מועד, דלא שייך מוקצה אלא (בנפל) בשבת וביו"ט, ומשום ביזוי מצוה לא הוה אסרינן להו היכא דנפלו. אבל השתא דאמרי' דאיתקצי וביזוי מצוה, אסרינן אפילו נפלו, ואפי' בחוה"מ. וקשה לר"י: כיון דנויי סוכה אסורין משום ביזוי, א"כ מאי פריך בביצה בפ' המביא (דף ל: ושם) מנויי סוכה אעצי סוכה, דקאמר: "וסוכת החג לא מהני בה תנאה? והתני' סככה כהלכתה כו'"? ומאי קושיא? דילמא עצי סוכה לא מהני ביה תנאה דמקרא נפקא, כדדריש התם: "מניין לעצי סוכה שאסורין כל שבעה? ת"ל: 'חג הסוכות ז' ימים וגו' '", ודרשה גמורה היא, כדמוכח בפ"ק דסוכה (דף ט. ושם), דב"ש פסלי מהאי קרא סוכה ישנה וב"ה מכשירין, דההוא מיבעי ליה לעצי סוכה שאסורין כל שבעה; אבל נויי סוכה, דלא אסירי אלא משום ביזוי, מהני בהו תנאה! ועוד, בפרק כירה (לקמן שבת דף מה.) משמע בהדיא דעצי סוכה לא אסור אלא משום דאיתקצאי למצותה! והשיב ר"ת: דבין נויי סוכה ובין עצי סוכה היתרים על הכשר סוכה לא אסירי אלא משום ביזוי או משום הואיל והוקצה למצותו, ולא אסירי מקרא אלא דווקא כדי הכשר סוכה. והמקשה דפריך בביצה (דך ל:) מנויי סוכה אעצי סוכה לא ידע שיש חילוק בין יותר מכדי הכשר סוכה לכדי הכשר סוכה. ומשני: באומר איני בודל מהם כל בה"ש, דלא חיילא קדושה על נויי סוכה; וכן על עצים היתרין על הכשר סוכה מהני בה תנאה. אבל עצי סוכה כדי הכשר, חיילא קדושה עלייהו על כרחו דבר תורה כל שבעה, ולא מהני תנאה. והא דקאמר התם: "ואם התנה עליהן הכל לפי תנאו", ופריך: "למימרא דמהני בה תנאה כו'", ומשני: "סיפא אתאן לסוכה דעלמא", ובתר הכי פריך: "וסוכת החג לא מהני בה תנאה? והתניא סככה כו'" — לא בעי לשנויי הכל לפי תנאו על יתרות מכדי הכשר סוכה, ד"הכל לפי תנאו" משמע בכל הסוכה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:1.english: Regarding a sukkah, it was taught [in a baraita] - This implies that the reason [for the prohibition against using] sukkah decorations is because of disparagement of a mitzvah [bizui mitzvah]. And the Ri finds this difficult: In chapter Kireh (below, Shabbat 45a, and Tosafot there), it implies that the reason is since it was set aside for its mitzvah [at twilight, it remains set aside for the entire duration] (migo de'itkatzai lemitzvatah)! And he answered that both [reasons] are necessary: For based [solely] on 'since it was set aside for its mitzvah,' we would not have prohibited them on Chol HaMoed, as muktzeh applies only (if it fell) on Shabbat and Yom Tov; and based [solely] on disparagement of a mitzvah, we would not have prohibited them where they fell down. But now that we say both that it was set aside and disparagement of a mitzvah, we prohibit them even if they fell down, and even on Chol HaMoed. And the Ri further asks: Since sukkah decorations are prohibited because of disparagement [of a mitzvah], if so, why does [the Gemara] in Beitzah, in the chapter [entitled] HaMevi (30b, and Tosafot there), raise an objection from sukkah decorations against the wood of a sukkah, as it says: "And is a stipulation not effective for a festival sukkah? But wasn't it taught: [If] one roofed it in accordance with its halakhic requirements..." etc.? And what is the objection? Perhaps for the wood of a sukkah a stipulation is not effective because it is derived from a verse, as [the Gemara] expounds there: "From where is it derived that the wood of a sukkah is prohibited all seven [days]? The verse states: 'The festival of Sukkot, seven days [to the Lord]'" (Leviticus 23:34). And this is an absolute exposition, as is proven in the first chapter of Sukkah (9a, and Tosafot there), where Beit Shammai invalidate an old sukkah based on this verse, and Beit Hillel validate [it] because they require that [verse] for [the law that] the wood of a sukkah is prohibited all seven days; whereas sukkah decorations, which are prohibited only because of disparagement [of a mitzvah], a stipulation should be effective for them! Furthermore, in chapter Kireh (below, Shabbat 45a), it implies explicitly that the wood of a sukkah is prohibited only because it was set aside for its mitzvah! And Rabbeinu Tam answered that both sukkah decorations and wood of the sukkah that are in excess of the valid minimum requirement of a sukkah are prohibited only because of disparagement [of a mitzvah] or because "since it was set aside for its mitzvah"; and they are not prohibited by the verse except specifically for the amount necessary for the valid minimum of the sukkah. And the questioner who raised the objection in Beitzah (30b) from sukkah decorations against the wood of a sukkah did not know that there is a distinction between [wood] in excess of the valid minimum requirement of a sukkah and the valid minimum requirement of a sukkah. And [the Gemara] resolves it [by establishing the baraita as referring to] where one says: "I do not withdraw from them for the entire twilight period," so that sanctity does not devolve upon the sukkah decorations; and similarly, for wood in excess of the valid minimum of a sukkah, a stipulation is effective for it. But for the wood of the sukkah of the valid minimum, sanctity devolves upon them perforce by Torah law for all seven days, and a stipulation is not effective. And as for that which [the Gemara] says there [in the first baraita]: "And if he stipulated concerning it, everything is according to his stipulation," and objects: "Is that to say that a stipulation is effective for it?..."; and answers: "The latter clause refers to an ordinary sukkah"; and after that objects: "And is a stipulation not effective for a festival sukkah? But wasn't it taught: [If] one roofed it... etc." — [why] did [the Gemara] not want to answer that "everything is according to his stipulation" [in the first baraita] refers to [wood] in excess of the valid minimum requirement of the sukkah? Because "everything is according to his stipulation" implies for the entire sukkah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:2.hebrew: אסור להסתפק מהן עד מוצאי יו"ט האחרון - והא דשרי אתרוג ביו"ט האחרון טפי מסוכה, מפרש בפרק לולב וערבה (סוכה מו:): משום דסוכה, בספק שביעי ספק שמיני יתובי יתבינן; ואי מתרמי ליה סעודה בין השמשות — אכיל ליה התם, והואיל ואיתקצי בין השמשות — איתקצי כוליה יומא של ספק ח' וט'. אבל אתרוג אינו ניטל בספק ז' וח', ולא איתסר בספק שמיני אלא משום דאיתקצי בין השמשות של ז'. ואע"פ דבין השמשות של ח' נמי אסור משום שהוא ספק יום, הואיל ולא אסור אלא משום ספק יום וספק לילה — לא איתקצי בכך כולי יומא; מידי דהוה אביצה שנולדה בזה דמותרת בזה, אע"פ דבין השמשות אסור משום ספק יום וספק לילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:2.english: "It is prohibited to use them until the conclusion of the last Festival day" - And that which an etrog is permitted on the last Festival day more than a sukka is explained in chapter Lulav Ve-Aravah (Sukkah 46b): Because regarding a sukka, on [the day that is] doubtful seventh [or] doubtful eighth [i.e., the eighth day in the Diaspora], we sit [in it]; and if a meal happens to present itself to him at twilight, he eats it there [in the sukka]. And since it was set aside at twilight, it was set aside for the entire day of doubtful eighth and ninth [i.e., the ninth day, Simchat Torah]. However, an etrog is not taken on [the day that is] doubtful seventh and eighth, and it was prohibited on doubtful eighth only because it was set aside during the twilight of the seventh [day]. And even though during the twilight of the eighth [day] it is also prohibited because it is doubtful daytime, since it is only prohibited because of doubtful day and doubtful night, it is not set aside thereby for the entire day — just as it is with an egg that was laid on this [Festival day], which is permitted on that [subsequent Festival day], even though during twilight it is prohibited because of doubtful day and doubtful night.

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:3.hebrew: אבוהון דכולהו דם - הא דלא קאמר "אבוהון דכולהו עצי סוכה", דנפקי מקרא, כדאמר בריש המביא בביצה (דף ל: ושם) — אומר ר"י, דמשום דמעצי סוכה לא הוה ילפינן; דשאני סוכה, דבמסתפק מהן איכא ביטול מצוה; אבל בנויי סוכה ובהרצאת מעות לאור נר חנוכה ליכא ביטול מצוה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:4:3.english: "The paradigm of them all is blood" - As for that which [Rav Yosef] did not say, "The paradigm of them all is the wood of the sukkah," which is derived from Scripture, as [the Gemara] states at the beginning of [the chapter] HaMevi in Beitzah (30b and there) — the Ri says that [this is] because we would not have derived [the rule] from the wood of the sukkah, for a sukkah is different, as in taking from them [for personal use] there is cancellation of the mitzvah; whereas with the decorations of the sukkah and with counting money by the light of the Hanukkah candle, there is no cancellation of the mitzvah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:5:1.hebrew: רב אמר אין מתירין מבגד לבגד - לא מבעיא אי חובת טלית הוא דאסור, אלא אפילו חובת גברא הוא נמי אסור — כדאשכחן במזוזה דנענש אותו שנטלה, בבבא מציעא בסוף פרק השואל (דף קב.), אף על גב דחובת הדר היא. ושמואל אמר "מתירין" — אע"ג דשמואל גופי' סבר דחובת טלית היא, אפ"ה מתירין, כיון שעושהו לצורך בגד אחר. וגבי מזוזה שנענש — שמא לא היה בדעתו להניח בבית אחר; א"נ, מזוזה שאני, שעשויה להציל מן המזיקין. ואע"ג דלכ"ע אין מתירין שלא להניח בבגד אחר, אין קשה מה שנהגו להתיר ציצית מטליתות של מתים — דדווקא בטלית של חי, שהוא בר חיובא, אין מתירין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:5:1.english: "Rav said: One may not untie [fringes] from [one] garment to [another] garment" - It is not necessary [to state that] if [the mitzvah of tzitzit] is an obligation of the garment, it is forbidden [to untie them], but even if it is an obligation of the person, it is also forbidden — as we find regarding a mezuzah, where the one who removed it was punished, in Bava Metzia at the end of the chapter [entitled] HaSho'el (102a), even though [a mezuzah] is an obligation of the resident. And Shmuel said: "One may untie [them]" — even though Shmuel himself maintains that it is an obligation of the garment, nevertheless one may untie [them], since he does so for the sake of another garment. And regarding the mezuzah, where [the person] was punished — perhaps he did not intend to place it in another house; alternatively, a mezuzah is different, because it is made to protect from harmful spirits. And even though according to everyone, one may not untie [fringes] without placing [them] on another garment, there is no difficulty from that which people are accustomed to untie fringes from the cloaks of the deceased — for it is specifically with the cloak of a living person, who is subject to obligation, that one may not untie [them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 22a:6:1.english: "In all matters of the Master [Rabba], he acted in accordance with Rav" - The difficulty from the first chapter of Ketubot (6a) is written there.
